t.n: Torre del Greco shell and coral carving
t.d: World centre of shell cameo carving and coral working near Naples.
t.tech: Shell blanks marked with ovals, cut and carved mainly with the bulino scraper, then oiled and polished
t.auth: Ultrasonic machine-cut agate cameos show a satin finish and no undercutting, markers appraisers use

t.d: Memorial jewellery holding hair or portraits, boosted by Queen Victoria's mourning for Prince Albert.
t.tech: Hairwork (braided or woven hair), black enamel, jet carving
t.mat: Whitby jet, French jet (black glass), onyx, ebonite, hair, gold
t.auth: Names or death dates on pieces from the 17th century on; French jet (black glass) and ebonite were cheaper substitutes for jet

t.d: Navajo silverwork begun by Atsidi Sani, known for stamped and cast cuffs set with turquoise.
t.tech: hammering coin or ingot silver, stamp work, chiselling, tufa casting, bezel setting
t.mat: silver (pesos, US coins, then refinery ingots), copper, brass, turquoise
t.auth: coin-derived silver, hand stamp and chisel marks, filed ingot grooves, Native-cut or domed turquoise in bezels

t.p: Heian period to present; peak late Edo
t.d: Japanese hair ornaments worn with traditional hairstyles, notably by geisha and maiko.
t.tech: lacquering, metalwork; tsumami (folded silk squares glued into flowers)
t.mat: lacquered wood, tortoiseshell, silk, gold- and silver-plated metal, bakelite
t.auth: hand-folded silk petals; seasonal motifs matching the month

t.p: ancient; flourished in the Mughal era
t.d: Gem setting in which gold foil is burnished between the stone and its mount, mainly for elaborate necklaces.
t.tech: ghaat framework, wax paadh, khudai stone fitting, meenakari, pakai foil setting, chillai polishing
t.mat: pure gold, gold foil, uncut diamonds, coloured gemstones; silver copies

t.d: Natural diamonds cleaved from rough and lightly polished, not faceted, set foil-backed in gold.
t.tech: kundan foil setting behind the stone; enamelled reverse
t.mat: natural uncut diamonds, 22–24K gold, gold foil
t.auth: genuine diamonds of irregular outline with flat foil-backed underside; meenakari reverse (a plain back suggests a shortcut piece)

t.p: peak under the Mughals, 16th–17th c.; Rajput courts 17th–18th c.; living
t.d: Prong-free setting of uncut and table-cut gems in gold, each stone locked by pressed kundan foil.
t.tech: 24K kundan foil pressed cold around each stone into a chased 18–22K gold body; stones set last; reverse enamelled
t.mat: gold, polki, table- and flat-cut diamonds, foiled coloured stones, carved gem panels
t.auth: no prongs; visible kundan border round each stone; enamelled reverse; flat-cut or uncut stones, not brilliants; watch for brilliant-cut replacements

t.p: Safavid style c. 15th c.; brought to India by the Mughals
t.d: Enamelling of metal by fusing coloured powdered glass onto the surface.
t.mat: gold, silver, copper; coloured glass enamel

t.p: traced to the Chola dynasty, 9th c. CE
t.d: Gold jewellery set with stones, first made to adorn temple deities and now worn by brides and Bharatanatyam dancers.
t.mat: gold; red and green kuchu kal (kemp) stones

t.p: Rajput era; invention credited to Nathu ji Soni, 1767 (unconfirmed)
t.d: Finely worked 23-carat gold sheet fused onto coloured glass.
t.tech: freehand etching of gold sheet on a lac base, fused onto treated glass
t.mat: 23K gold sheet, coloured glass, lac resin
ctr: Raj-Soni family (Mahesh Raj Soni, Padma Shri 2015)

t.d: Silver filigree made from fine drawn wire shaped and soldered by hand.
t.tech: silver cast into rod, drawn into wire, hand-shaped and soldered with borax; granulation

t.r: Zuni Pueblo, New Mexico, United States
t.d: Zuni jewellery known for inlaid stone patterns and delicate needlepoint and petit point turquoise clusters.
t.tech: stone inlay; clusterwork with needle-shaped (needlepoint) or small shaped (petit point) stones set in silver
t.mat: silver, turquoise, mother-of-pearl, shell, coral, lapis, jet, onyx

t.d: Hopi silver style of a cut-out top sheet soldered over a darkened base, developed with the Museum of Northern Arizona.
t.tech: overlay: design cut from one silver sheet and soldered onto a second, background oxidised

t.d: Tuareg smiths of Niger casting silver pendants such as the Agadez cross, also worn by neighbouring Songhai, Zarma, Fulani and Hausa.
Amazigh jewellery of Kabylie known for cloisonné enamel in yellow, green and blue on silver, with coral.
t.tech: cloisonné enamelling, possibly brought by jewellers exiled from Muslim Spain

t.d: Openwork lattice crosses of the Ethiopian Orthodox Church, no two alike; neck, hand and processional forms.
Carving of New Zealand pounamu into taonga such as hei-tiki, hei matau and pekapeka.
t.tech: abrasive rubbing, shaping with sticks and water, long polishing
t.auth: Pounamu is found only in New Zealand; much souvenir 'greenstone' is imported jade.

t.d: Galway goldsmiths' continuous making of the Claddagh ring since at least 1700, marketed widely from the 19th century.
